headline: Simple Treatments Beat High-Tech Options for Knee Arthritis
meta_description: Nearly 10,000 patients show knee braces, water therapy, and exercise outperform ultrasound and other advanced treatments for osteoarthritis pain.
summary_short: A major analysis of nearly 10,000 patients reveals that simple therapies like knee braces and water exercise work better than high-tech options.
body:
A sweeping analysis of 139 clinical trials involving nearly 10,000 patients has revealed an encouraging truth: some of the most effective treatments for knee osteoarthritis are also among the simplest and most accessible. Knee braces ranked highest overall for reducing pain and stiffness while improving mobility, while water-based therapy proved especially powerful for pain relief, and regular exercise consistently delivered benefits for both pain and physical function. The research, led by Yuan Luo of the First People's Hospital of Neijiang, China, and published in the open-access journal PLOS One, compared 12 different non-drug approaches—from laser therapy to ultrasound—using a network meta-analysis that allowed researchers to rank treatments across many different studies.

The findings challenge the assumption that newer, more technologically advanced interventions necessarily perform better. Ultrasound, despite its high-tech reputation, repeatedly ranked near the bottom of comparisons. Even high-intensity laser therapy and shock wave therapy, while showing promise in certain areas, did not outperform the simpler physical therapies. This matters enormously for the millions of older adults living with knee osteoarthritis, because traditional anti-inflammatory medications carry gastrointestinal and cardiovascular risks that many patients wish to avoid.

The researchers acknowledge that their rankings have limitations—the 139 studies varied in design, some involved small participant groups, and treatment durations differed. Yet they conclude that physical therapies represent genuinely promising alternatives to medication. Future research will explore whether combining treatments yields even better results and which approaches offer the greatest benefits relative to their cost. For patients seeking relief without pharmaceutical side effects, the message is clear: a knee brace, time in warm water, and consistent movement may be exactly what the body needs.
quick_facts: Knee braces ranked highest for pain and mobility
Water therapy especially effective for pain relief
Ultrasound performed worst among 12 treatments tested
Research led by Yuan Luo, First People's Hospital of Neijiang, China
